subject: Parklane Medical — next steps & ops runbook for reserved GPU pilot
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Parklane Medical — discovery recap & proposed reserved GPU pilot

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the clear overview of Parklane's inference bottlenecks. Writing up a short recap + concrete next steps so we can align on scope for a reserved GPU pilot. Attachments: redwood-pilot-runbook-v1.pdf (ops runbook) and SLA-terms-draft.docx (high-level terms).

Quick summary of what I heard:
- Pain points:
  - Unpredictable latency during batch reports and morning surge windows (you called out 6-8x latency variance).
  - Current infra (on-prem K8s + Triton) struggles to scale predictably without manual intervention.
  - Strong requirement for workload isolation and HIPAA-compliant controls.
- Current stack and constraints:
  - Models served: ensemble of a 7B conversational model (primary) + a smaller 1.3B reranker.
  - Typical peak: ~600 TPS for short-form inference (sub-1024 tokens); occasional long-form jobs up to 2048 tokens for summaries.
  - Ops: internal SRE team has limited experience with GPU autoscaling policies for bursty traffic.
- Success criteria for a pilot (what will make this successful for Parklane):
  1) 95th/99th p99 latency under 200ms for short requests at peak TPS.
  2) Predictable throughput (able to sustain 600 TPS with <10% variance across windows).
  3) Isolated environment (no shared customer data on inference nodes) and encryption-in-transit/rest matches your controls.

What we propose for the reserved GPU pilot (initial recommendation):
- Reserved pool: min=4 GPU equivalents, baseline node config tuned for your 7B model.
- Burst policy: allow autoscale up to 8 GPUs for sustained bursts (recommended burst window 30-45 mins).
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to a quantized 4-bit variant if the pool hits max capacity (keeps service available with graceful degradation).
- Prefill/warm-up: background prefill of KV cache for expected morning sequences to avoid cold-start penalty.

Next steps / asks (short timeline):
1) We share the attached runbook + SLA draft (attached). Please confirm any regulatory controls we must include. (Action: Rachel — today)
2) Security contact: please add the person from your Security team so we can send the SOC2 + encryption details.
3) Ops call to lock in autoscale parameters and start date — propose Wed 9/15 10:00am PT or Thu 9/16 2:00pm PT.
4) If you confirm, we’ll scope a 4-week pilot with a mid-pilot check at week 2 to validate p99 targets.

Happy to adjust any of the above — if useful I can include a sample metric dashboard and runbook checklist in the ops call.

Thanks,
Rachel

Thanks, Rachel — useful summary. Couple quick clarifications before we lock dates: 

- p99 target: the 200ms target is for our short inference path (<=512 tokens). For the 2048 token jobs we can tolerate up to 700ms but we want predictable SLAs.
- Warm-up: how do you recommend we prefilling KV cache — is that a one-time warm-up or ongoing background process?
- Model variants: are quantized variants compatible with our accuracy bar? We can tolerate some small delta but not >2% BLEU/ROUGE drop for summaries.
- Data residency: we need processing to occur in US East region and logs retained for 90 days.

Please include my security lead (Aisha is looped) on the ops materials. Wed 9/15 10am PT works for me.

-Sam

CTO, Parklane Medical

Sam — great, thanks for the quick reply and for confirming the 9/15 slot. Short answers below and I updated the runbook to call out the items you asked about (see attached v1 -> v1.1 at the ops call).

- p99 targets: understood — we’ll validate 200ms for <=512 tokens and include a separate SLA line for long-form jobs (<=2048 tokens) with a p99 <=700ms.
- KV cache warm-up: Recommend an automated warm-up job that runs 30–60 minutes before known surge windows (we can schedule by cron or trigger via your traffic forecast). For unpredictable bursts we keep a small standing cache and optimize continuous batching to reduce cold starts.
- Quantized variant accuracy: We’ll run an evaluation using your sample prompt set (please share a redacted set). In our experience, well-tuned 4-bit quantization for transformers of this size typically yields <1.5% ROUGE degradation with per-task tuning. We’ll include an evaluation plan in the pilot scope.
- Data residency & logs: US East processing is fine — we’ll ensure node placement and S3-like object storage retention is set to 90 days. Full audit logs will be available for the duration of the pilot.

Concrete technical proposal (short):
- Baseline pool: 4 H100-class GPUs (reserved).
- Autoscale: min=4, max=8. Scale trigger: queue depth + token throughput; cooldown=90s; allow burst up to 45 mins for scheduled windows (we’ll enforce via policy).
- Routing/fallback: quantized model variant (4-bit) routed automatically when queue length exceeds threshold — this preserves availability and reduces tail latency.
- Monitoring: per-token latency, p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, batch size distribution, cache hit rate.

Ops call: I’ll send a calendar invite for Wed 9/15 10:00am PT with a short agenda (rollout timeline, runbook review, security checklist, pilot go/no-go criteria). Please bring: a sample prompt set for the eval, and your security contact (Aisha).

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Rachel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
